sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area/Volume
lecture_lines: Determinants measure the signed area of parallelograms.
This parallelogram is formed by the matrix column vectors.
Transformation scales the area by the determinant.
animations: Draw a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg] on a 2D plane with vertices at origin, v1, v2, and v1+v2; fill it with #FF0000.
Label the column vectors v1 and v2 in #FFFF00 and highlight them.
Animate a transformation that stretches the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg] and changes its area, showing the factor as |det(A)|.

sections.title: The Linear System as Vector Scaling
lecture_lines: Consider the linear system Ax equals b.
We interpret this as a vector combination.
The goal is to reach point b.
animations: Display the equation Ax = b in white.
Visualize vector A as column vectors a1 and a2; show x1*a1 + x2*a2 = b.
Draw a vector b as a target point [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/target.svg] on the 2D plane [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/plane.svg] in #00FF00.

sections.title: Geometric Derivation of Cramer's Rule
lecture_lines: Replace a column of A with b.
This creates a new, scaled parallelogram.
The area ratio reveals the specific coordinate.
This geometric change isolates each coordinate value.
We define Cramer's Rule using these areas.
animations: Replace column a1 in matrix A with vector b to form A1.
Show a new [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg] formed by b and a2; color it #0000FF.
Display the ratio of areas: det(A1) / det(A) = x1.
Animate the transition showing how area ratio corresponds to x1 coordinate.
Summarize the rule x_i = det(Ai) / det(A) in #FFFFFF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg].

sections.title: Synthesizing the Formula
lecture_lines: We formalize this as a simple formula.
Coordinate x equals the ratio of determinants.
The determinant acts as a scaling factor.
Both views match perfectly in theory.
Visual intuition matches the algebraic definition.
animations: Display the equation x = det(Ai) / det(A) in a bold white box.
Highlight the x1 = det(A1) / det(A) component in #00FFFF.
Use an arrow animation to show how determinant scales the unit square.
Compare the geometric parallelogram area with the algebraic result.
Flash the final formula in #FF00FF to emphasize completeness.

sections.title: Constraints and Summary
lecture_lines: What if the determinant equals zero?
The area collapses to a line.
Cramer's Rule fails for singular matrices.
animations: Show det(A) = 0 and illustrate the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg] collapsing to a line.
Animate the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg] squashing into a 1D line segment.
Display 'Cramer's Rule Fails' in bright #FF4500 when det(A) is zero.
